Fixed events: homeward after knighting to obtain supplies and a squire; cries in the oak thicket; Juan Haldudo releases Andrés under a lance threat; nine months at seven reals, sixty-three owed; deductions refused; Andrés warns against being left; promise accepted; Quixote departs; Juan beats Andrés worse and releases him unpaid; Quixote congratulates himself; Rocinante chooses the homeward road; six Toledo traders bound for Murcia demand evidence of Dulcinea’s beauty; mocking portrait proposal; charge fails when horse stumbles; muleteer breaks lance and beats fallen Quixote despite merchants’ protests; Pedro Alonso finds, recognizes, tends and brings neighbour home on donkey; Baldwin/Abindarráez identifications; discreet arrival after dusk; worried household blames books; ten-giants claim; food and sleep. No chapter-6 book burning or Sancho joining yet.

Only “I know who I am,” is a direct Ormsby quotation. Other dialogue is original modern adaptation. Student helper, choices, classroom, magical journal window, extra questions and private conversations are invented connective material. Seven binary choices affect replies, attention and bounded callbacks; never the source outcomes. Pedro remains the rescuer. The journal window allows reader knowledge of Andrés’s aftermath without giving Quixote that knowledge.

Non-graphic treatment: no blows against Andrés are animated; his clothing is retained. The second beating is described with the page dark, then its outcome stated. Quixote’s fall and the muleteer’s violence are stylized/narrated. Mounted travel, horse, armour, shield, ropes and donkey are described rather than visibly rigged. Quixote’s existing brown costume is a theatrical stand-in; the new lance is a visible attached prop. It is explicitly cleared after the fall and before its destruction. A low crouched pose suggests the fallen state, not a new canonical recovery.
